t: Israel: Eisenkot poised to form the next government
s: Parties representing 67 lawmakers recommended Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu. President Isaac Herzog was due to assign the mandate on Sunday, November 8.

t: Poland: six killed in a shooting in Kraków
s: A gunman opened fire on Saturday, November 7, in Kraków's main square, killing six people and wounding about fifteen before being shot and wounded by police. Authorities say he acted alone and held ultranationalist views.

t: United States: Democrats retake Congress
s: Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, according to projections. Several seats were still to be called.

t: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Argentina
s: According to the schedule released by the Vatican, the pope leaves Uruguay for Argentina on November 8 (Buenos Aires, Córdoba, Luján) before ending his tour in Peru from November 11 to 17. No pope had visited Argentina since 1987.

t: EU leaders to meet in Dublin on November 13
s: An informal meeting of EU heads of state and government takes place in Dublin on November 13, the day after the European Political Community summit, held in the same city on November 12.

t: Wages: social conference on Monday at Matignon
s: Following the November 5 protests, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is meeting unions and employers on Monday, November 9. Labour Minister Jean-Pierre Farandou wants to lift the net minimum wage above €1,500 a month; the CFDT union is asking for an extra €100 net, the CGT for a 10% raise.

t: A wave of hoax bomb threats in European skies
s: At least twenty flights were targeted on Thursday, November 5, and all landed safely. In France, the Évreux prosecutor opened an investigation into the pilot of an Aer Lingus flight who allegedly refused to land at the Évreux military air base.

t: 2027 presidential race: LFI unveils Mélenchon's platform
s: La France insoumise presented the new version of Jean-Luc Mélenchon's platform on November 6 and 7, with a rally in Le Bourget. Ecology becomes its cornerstone.

t: Besançon: 13 arrests after a jewellery factory heist
s: Thirteen suspects were arrested after the armed robbery of a jewellery factory in Besançon, France's national anti-organised-crime prosecutor said on November 4.

t: Wall Street: the Nasdaq 100 has its worst day since 2020
s: On Thursday, November 5, the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36%, the S&P 500 lost 4.35% and the Dow Jones dropped 1,833 points. Investors sold memory-chip, storage, chip-equipment and data-centre stocks.

t: US jobs: 165,000 added in October
s: The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than expected, and the unemployment rate stands at 4.1%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

t: Fed: a December rate hike looks increasingly likely
s: After the jobs report, CME's FedWatch tool put the probability of a quarter-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December at 76.8%.

t: OpenAI unveils GPT-6 Cyber, a vulnerability-hunting model
s: Restricted to vetted security teams, the model found 81 serious flaws in Firefox and produced 948 exploits for Linux kernel flaws, which were reported to maintainers, according to figures released by OpenAI.

t: FlashProve: proving which AI model produced an answer
s: Anthropic open-sourced FlashProve, a research prototype that cryptographically proves a response came from a given model without revealing its weights. The system remains costly and is not deployed in any product.

t: Dropbox buys Tigris Data for $350 million
s: Dropbox will acquire Tigris Data, a start-up specialising in storage for AI applications, for about $350 million in cash. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter.

t: Blight-resistant rice thanks to an AI-designed tool
s: University of Missouri researchers made rice plants resistant to bacterial blight, a disease that threatens harvests in Asia and Africa, using OpenCRISPR-1, an AI-designed, freely usable gene-editing tool. Published in the journal aBIOTECH, the work is at the lab stage: commercial varieties are several years away.

t: Measles: nearly 4,900 US cases this year
s: The CDC counted 4,852 measles cases as of October 29, 264 more than in its previous update. 96% of patients were unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status.

t: COP31 opens on Monday in Antalya
s: The UN climate conference runs from November 9 to 20 in Türkiye. Murat Kurum presides, and Australia's Chris Bowen leads the negotiations.

t: Champions League: Lens thrashed 9-1 by Como
s: On Wednesday, November 4 at Bollaert, Lens suffered the heaviest defeat ever for a French club in European competition. No team had ever conceded nine goals at home in the Champions League.

t: Israel: Eisenkot tasked with forming the government
s: President Isaac Herzog on Sunday gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form the next government, after the October 27 election. He has 28 days, extendable by 14, and promises a “national emergency government”.

t: Ukraine: massive Russian strikes ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks
s: Volodymyr Zelensky accuses Russia of stepping up strikes on the power grid to gain leverage before the US-brokered negotiations in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. Moscow launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, including North Korean-supplied KN-23s.

t: Pope Leo XIV welcomed to Argentina by Javier Milei
s: Arriving in Buenos Aires on Sunday, the pope called for democracy to be protected and said the economy must serve people, not the other way around, a veiled critique of Javier Milei's austerity policy according to the AP. He will then travel on to Peru.

t: Wages: social conference at Matignon today
s: Sébastien Lecornu is meeting the leaders of the main unions and employer organisations today on purchasing power and wages, following the November 5 protests. The minimum wage is at the heart of the talks: the CFDT union wants an extra €100 net.

t: Tokyo: the Nikkei drops almost 6% on Friday
s: The Tokyo Stock Exchange closed down 5.96% on Friday at 57,434.77 points, dragged down by technology stocks. The Topix lost 5.9%.

t: OpenAI raises $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
s: OpenAI has closed a first tranche of about $11 billion in a round that could reach $20 billion, at a $1.25 trillion valuation, according to Bloomberg. The company has not announced it officially.

t: COP31 opens in Antalya with lowered ambitions
s: The UN climate conference opens today in Antalya, Türkiye, and runs until November 20. According to Bloomberg, its agenda is narrower than at previous COPs and ambitions have been scaled back.

t: Route du Rhum: Tom Laperche wins in record time
s: Tom Laperche (SVR-Lazartigue) won the Route du Rhum in the Ultim class overnight from Saturday to Sunday, in 6 days, 13 hours and 27 minutes. He beat the record set by Charles Caudrelier in 2022 by more than six hours.

t: F1: Lando Norris wins the São Paulo Grand Prix
s: The McLaren driver won Sunday's race at Interlagos, ahead of Max Verstappen, who climbed from 21st place, and Isack Hadjar.

t: Ligue 1: Marseille win 2-1 at Lens
s: Marseille won on Sunday at Bollaert, four days after Lens's rout against Como. Amine Gouiri opened the scoring in the 2nd minute, Florian Thauvin equalised, and Keyliane Abdallah gave OM the win in the 82nd.

t: Kraków: the gunman dies in hospital
s: The gunman who killed six people and wounded fifteen on Saturday, November 7, in Kraków's main square died in hospital on Monday, according to police. He had been wounded by officers during the attack. Authorities describe a far-right-inspired attack.

t: Ukraine: Europeans join the Abu Dhabi talks
s: European officials are set to take part this week in the US-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. The Kremlin objected, saying the negotiations are strictly trilateral.

t: Trump says his deportations were “too tough” after the midterms
s: In an interview aired on Sunday, November 8, Donald Trump said his deportation policy had been too tough and hurt him in the midterm elections. He said he was open to an immigration deal with Democrats.

t: Minimum wage to rise 1.6% from December 1
s: Following the social conference at Matignon on Monday, November 9, Sébastien Lecornu announced an early increase in the minimum wage (Smic), to €1,502 net a month on December 1. Unions say the rise is insufficient, and the CGT is calling a strike on November 17.

t: Paris stocks rebound as oil prices fall
s: The CAC 40 gained 1.16% on Monday, November 9, to 8,233.30 points, supported by falling crude prices. STMicroelectronics led the index with a 5.30% gain.

t: Nvidia falls after an investigation targeting CEO Jensen Huang
s: Nvidia shares fell about 4% on Monday, November 9. On Sunday, the board opened an independent investigation into Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive suspected by US intelligence of spying for China. The company says it has no reason to believe its secrets were compromised.

t: COP31: opening in Antalya amid a finance dispute
s: The UN climate conference opened on Monday, November 9, in Antalya. Rich and developing countries clashed from the outset over climate finance, delaying the adoption of the agenda.

t: WMO: 2015-2026, the twelve warmest years on record
s: In its update published for COP31, the World Meteorological Organization says 2015-2026 will be the warmest twelve-year period on record. The years 2023 to 2026 are the four warmest in the observational record.

t: Ligue 1: Lille win 2-1 at Rennes and climb to second
s: LOSC won 2-1 at Stade Rennais on Sunday, November 8, in the 10th round, and moved up to second place in the table.

t: Ligue 1: Brest beat Lyon 2-0
s: Stade Brestois beat Olympique Lyonnais 2-0 on Sunday, November 8, in the 10th round. It was Lyon's first match since Paulo Fonseca's departure.

t: Ukraine: Russians, Ukrainians and Americans meet in Abu Dhabi
s: Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations opened a new round of US-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, November 10, with the United States represented by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. According to The Washington Post, European security is on the agenda, after Jared Kushner proposed a new security architecture involving Russia and European countries.

t: Education: teachers, pupils and students strike again
s: The joint union front for state schools and higher education, joined by high-school and student organisations, called a new day of strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday, November 10, following one on November 5. It is demanding more resources for schools and universities; a further day of action has been announced for November 17.

t: CAC 40 gains 0.55% as oil prices fall
s: The Paris stock exchange closed up 0.55% at 8,278.59 points on Tuesday, November 10, supported by lower oil prices. The index did, however, pare its gains after the release of US inflation figures for October.

t: Nexperia swamped as AI soaks up chipmaking capacity
s: Dutch semiconductor maker Nexperia is "totally oversubscribed", its interim CEO told Reuters on Tuesday at the Electronica trade fair in Munich. Suppliers are shifting capacity towards AI data centres, at the expense of the mature chips used in cars and industrial equipment.

t: Google adds two AI chips to its eighth-generation TPU line
s: Google unveiled two new versions of its in-house AI chips on Tuesday, November 10, the TPU 8tx and the TPU 8i Max, adding to the eighth generation launched in April. The TPU 8i Max combines two TPU 8i chips in a single package.

t: Women's Champions League: PSG beaten 1-2 by Bayern
s: PSG lost 1-2 to Bayern Munich at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday, November 10, on matchday four of the league phase. Trailing 2-0 at half-time, the Paris side pulled one back through a Paulina Dudek penalty.

t: Women's Champions League: Paris FC outclassed in Madrid (3-0)
s: Paris FC lost 3-0 away to Real Madrid on Tuesday, November 10, on matchday four of the league phase. After a goalless first half, the Madrid side scored three times after the break.

t: Ukraine: Moscow and Kyiv agree on a large prisoner exchange
s: Three-way talks with the United States ended in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday 11 November. Russia and Ukraine agreed on a major exchange of prisoners of war, with no exact figure yet. US envoy Jared Kushner hailed a humanitarian breakthrough, but no progress was announced towards a peace deal.

t: Emmanuel Macron leads his last Armistice Day ceremony
s: On Wednesday 11 November, Emmanuel Macron led the ceremony for the 108th anniversary of the 1918 Armistice in Paris, for the last time as head of state. He laid a wreath at the statue of Clemenceau, then rekindled the flame of the Unknown Soldier under the Arc de Triomphe. In his speech, he said the memory of 11 November belongs in every school, amid a debate among teachers.

t: The CAC 40 gains 0.66% in a public-holiday session
s: On Wednesday 11 November, the CAC 40 rose 0.66% to 8,332.87 points, up 54.28 points on the previous day. Volumes were thin in Paris, with 11 November a public holiday.

t: COP31: Guterres calls for a climate justice pact
s: Addressing leaders gathered in Antalya for COP31, UN Secretary-General António Guterres proposed a "climate justice compact". It aims to help developing countries move away from fossil fuels and protect those already suffering from climate change. He also suggested taxing fossil fuel companies to help the hardest-hit countries.

t: Global fossil CO2 emissions set to fall in 2026
s: According to Global Carbon Budget 2026 data, global fossil CO2 emissions are expected to fall by 0.41% this year. The decline would come from oil (−1.89%), while coal-related emissions would rise (+0.57%). The fall does not necessarily mean that emissions have peaked.
